# Research focus

This exploratory project describes early-pregnancy CYP24A1 expression in relation
to baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D, subsequent preeclampsia outcome and a derived
vitamin D group. CYP24A1 is related to vitamin D metabolism. The threshold of
30 ng/mL follows the source study; it is not a universal diagnostic threshold.
The continuous variable is `mat_vitD`. The categorical variables are
`preg_preeclampsia` and `vitD_group`, the latter derived from `mat_vitD`.

# step1 : Global settings and packages

The expression columns and covariate rows have different input orders.
All matching below uses sample identifiers. All 157 samples are retained;
no covariate or supplied expression value is missing.

```{r prepare-data}
# Load packages for data manipulation and visualization.
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

```

# Step2 : Import raw data

```{r}

# Import gene expression data and use the first column as row names.

cov_path <- "E:/桌面/raw/GSE85307_covar-1.csv"
expr_path <- "E:/桌面/raw/GSE85307_geneExpression.csv"
gene_path <- "E:/桌面/raw/GSE85307_geneNames.csv"

# Read input files from the project's data/raw folder.

#cov_path <- "data/raw/GSE85307_covar-1.csv"
#expr_path <- "data/raw/GSE85307_geneExpression.csv"
#gene_path <- "data/raw/GSE85307_geneNames.csv"



# Check file existence: TRUE means found; FALSE means not found.
file.exists(cov_path)
file.exists(expr_path)
file.exists(gene_path)

# Import participant characteristics.
covar_raw <- read.csv(
  cov_path,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Import gene expression data, using the first column as row names.
expr_raw <- read.csv(
  expr_path,
  row.names = 1,
  check.names = FALSE
)
# Import the probe-to-gene mapping table.
link_raw <- read.csv(
  gene_path,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Check dimensions: number of rows followed by number of columns.
dim(covar_raw)
dim(expr_raw)
dim(link_raw)
```

# step3 : Clean covariates

```{r}

# Define a function to remove the first label and trim whitespace.
strip_label <- function(x) trimws(sub("^[^:]*:\\s*", "", x, perl = TRUE))

# Create a working copy and retain the raw data object.
clean <- covar_raw

# Remove labels from variables other than participant identifiers.
for (v in setdiff(names(clean), c("subjectID", "geoID"))) {
  clean[[v]] <- strip_label(clean[[v]])
}


# Identify variables that should be numeric.
num_vars <- c("mat_age_yrs", "delivery_gestAge_wks",
              "sampleCollection_gestAge_wks", "mat_BMI", "mat_vitD")


# Convert each variable and check for newly introduced missing values.
for (v in num_vars) {
  # Retain the values before conversion.
  before <- clean[[v]]
  # Convert text to numeric values.
  clean[[v]] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(before))
   # Stop if conversion turns a previously nonmissing value into NA.
  if (any(is.na(clean[[v]]) & !is.na(before))) stop("Numeric conversion failed: ", v)
}


```

# Step4 ：Validate identifiers and match samples

```{r}

# Check identifiers, probe IDs, and gene names for duplicates.
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(clean$geoID), !anyDuplicated(clean$subjectID),
          !anyDuplicated(colnames(expr_raw)), !anyDuplicated(rownames(expr_raw)),
          !anyDuplicated(link_raw$PROBEID), !anyDuplicated(link_raw$GENE),
          # Check whether both files contain the same set of samples.
          setequal(clean$geoID, colnames(expr_raw)),
          # Check that categorical variables contain only expected values.
          all(clean$preg_preeclampsia %in% c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")),
          all(clean$mat_asthma %in% c("0", "1")))
# Convert expression data to a matrix.
expr <- as.matrix(expr_raw)
# Check that all expression values are numeric and finite.
stopifnot(is.numeric(expr), all(is.finite(expr)))

# Reorder expression columns to match the covariate sample order.
expr <- expr[, match(clean$geoID, colnames(expr)), drop = FALSE]
# Confirm exact agreement of sample identifiers and order.
stopifnot(identical(colnames(expr), clean$geoID))
# Reorder the mapping table to match expression probe order.
map <- link_raw[match(rownames(expr), as.character(link_raw$PROBEID)), ]

# Check that each probe has a valid matching gene name.
stopifnot(!anyNA(map$GENE), identical(as.character(map$PROBEID), rownames(expr)))

# Replace probe row names with gene names.
rownames(expr) <- map$GENE

```

# Step5 : Create groups and combine data

```{r}

# Define categorical variables and their display order.
clean <- clean %>% mutate(
  # Pregnancy outcome: display Normal first.
  preg_preeclampsia = factor(preg_preeclampsia, levels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")),
  # Group vitamin D using the source study's 30 ng/mL threshold.
  vitD_group = factor(ifelse(mat_vitD < 30, "<30 ng/mL", ">=30 ng/mL"),
                      levels = c("<30 ng/mL", ">=30 ng/mL")),
  # Convert asthma codes to readable labels.
  mat_asthma = factor(mat_asthma, levels = c("0", "1"), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
  # Treat microarray batch as a categorical variable.
  batch_Microarray = factor(batch_Microarray))
# Transpose expression data to one sample per row and one gene per column.
all_genes <- as.data.frame(t(expr), check.names = FALSE)
# Combine covariates and expression after verifying sample order.
analysis_data <- bind_cols(clean, all_genes)
# Check the target gene and expected sample size.
stopifnot(
  "CYP24A1" %in% rownames(expr),
  nrow(analysis_data) == 157L
)

```

# Step6 ： Print concise data checks

```{r}

# Count missing values in each covariate.
missing_table <- data.frame(variable = names(clean), missing = colSums(is.na(clean)))


# Report sample size, expression rows, and outcome group counts.
data.frame(
  participants = nrow(clean),
  probes = nrow(expr),
  normal = sum(clean$preg_preeclampsia == "Normal"),
  preeclampsia = sum(clean$preg_preeclampsia == "Preeclampsia"),
  missing_covariate_values = sum(missing_table$missing)
)

# Count participants in each outcome and vitamin D subgroup.
group_counts <- analysis_data %>%
  count(
    preg_preeclampsia,
    vitD_group,
    .drop = FALSE
  )

# Print subgroup counts without printing the full dataset.
group_counts


```


```{r}
# Verify that no covariate values are missing.
stopifnot(
  sum(missing_table$missing) == 0
)

```

The missing-value check passed, confirming that none of the covariate values in the cleaned dataset were missing. Therefore, no participants needed to be excluded because of missing covariate data.


# Figure 1: Expression distribution

```{r histogram, fig.cap="Distribution of CYP24A1 expression among 157 participants, using 24 bins. The supplied expression scale is retained."}
# Plot a histogram of CYP24A1 expression.
p_hist <- ggplot(analysis_data, aes(CYP24A1)) +
  
  # Use 24 bins; bar heights represent participant counts.
  
  geom_histogram(bins = 24, fill = "#337C8E", colour = "white") +
  
  # Add a title, dynamic sample size, and axis labels.
  
  labs(title = "CYP24A1 expression distribution", subtitle = "n = 157",
       x = "CYP24A1 expression (provided scale)", y = "Number of participants") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)

# Display the plot.
p_hist
```
## Interpretation figure1

Among the 157 participants, CYP24A1 expression is approximately unimodal and centered around 4.8 on the supplied expression scale. The distribution shows slight right skewness, with a few relatively high values extending to approximately 5.2. Most observations fall between approximately 4.6 and 5.0. The histogram alone is insufficient to establish normality.


# Figure 2: Continuous vitamin D and expression

```{r scatterplot, fig.cap="Baseline vitamin D and CYP24A1 expression. The shaded band is the model-based 95% confidence interval for the unadjusted fitted mean, not a prediction interval."}
# Map continuous vitamin D to x and CYP24A1 expression to y.
p_scatter <- ggplot(analysis_data, aes(mat_vitD, CYP24A1)) +
  # Each point represents one participant; transparency reduces overlap.
  geom_point(colour = "#337C8E", alpha = .65, size = 1.7) +
  # Add an unadjusted linear fit and a 95% confidence band for the mean.
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE,
              colour = "#B65E27", fill = "#E4B48B", linewidth = .8) +
  # Set the title and axis labels
  labs(title = "CYP24A1 and baseline vitamin D", subtitle = "n = 157",
       x = "Baseline 25(OH)D (ng/mL)", y = "CYP24A1 expression (provided scale)") +
  # Use the same theme as Figure 1.
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)

# Display the plot.
p_scatter
```
## Interpretation - figure 2

The scatterplot shows little apparent linear association between baseline 25(OH)D and CYP24A1 expression. The unadjusted fitted line has a slight downward slope, but expression values vary considerably at similar vitamin D levels. The 95% confidence band widens at higher vitamin D levels, where observations are sparse, indicating greater uncertainty in the fitted mean. This plot does not establish a causal relationship or rule out nonlinear associations.

# Figure 3: Both categorical covariates

```{r boxplot, fig.width=8.2, fig.cap="CYP24A1 expression by subsequent pregnancy outcome and vitamin D group. Boxes show the median and interquartile range; Whiskers extend to the most extreme observed values within 1.5 times the IQR below the first quartile and above the third quartile. Jitter changes only horizontal display positions."}
# Count participants in each subgroup for plot annotations.
counts <- analysis_data %>% count(preg_preeclampsia, vitD_group)

# Position count labels above the highest expression value.
counts$label_y <- max(analysis_data$CYP24A1) + .05

# Map outcome to x, expression to y, and vitamin D group to fill.

p_box <- ggplot(analysis_data, aes(preg_preeclampsia, CYP24A1, fill = vitD_group)) +
  # Draw boxplots; individual points are shown in the next layer.
  
  geom_boxplot(width = .55, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = .65) +
  # Show each participant with horizontal jitter only.
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = .12, height = 0, seed = 103),
             shape = 21, size = 1.3, alpha = .6) +
  
  # Display the sample size above each subgroup.
  
  geom_text(data = counts, aes(x = preg_preeclampsia, y = label_y,
                             label = paste0("n = ", n)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.1) +
  # Create one panel for each vitamin D group.
  facet_wrap(~vitD_group) +
  # Specify fill colors for the two groups.
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#337C8E", "#D5A13B")) +
  # Add space for points and count labels.
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(.07, .17))) +
  
  # Set the title and axis labels.
  labs(title = "CYP24A1 by outcome and vitamin D group", subtitle = "n = 157",
       x = "Pregnancy outcome", y = "CYP24A1 expression (provided scale)") +
  # Keep a consistent theme and omit the redundant legend.
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
# Display the plot.
p_box
```

## Interpretation figure3

In the <30 ng/mL vitamin D group, participants with normal pregnancy outcomes (n = 78) and those who developed preeclampsia (n = 41) have similar median CYP24A1 expression and substantially overlapping distributions. In the ≥30 ng/mL group, participants who developed preeclampsia (n = 6) have a slightly lower observed median and a narrower interquartile range than those with normal outcomes (n = 32). However, this comparison should be interpreted cautiously because the preeclampsia subgroup contains only six participants. These descriptive differences do not establish statistical significance or causality.


# Conclusion

Overall, CYP24A1 expression shows little apparent linear association with baseline vitamin D. Expression distributions overlap across pregnancy outcome groups, although the small preeclampsia subgroup in the higher vitamin D category limits interpretation. These findings are exploratory.
